stories.headline: Ranchi airport cancels 20 flights as Cyclone Akvan cuts visibility
stories.title: Ranchi airport cancels 20 flights as Cyclone Akvan cuts visibility
stories.summary: Bad weather linked to Cyclone Akvan forced the cancellation of 20 scheduled flights at Ranchi airport
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: - Bad weather linked to Cyclone Akvan forced the cancellation of 20 scheduled flights at Ranchi airport, including six Air India Express services.
- Four flights were diverted as visibility fell below the 1,200–1,500 metres required for take-offs and landings, according to airport officials.
- The India Meteorological Department expects skies to start clearing on Sunday, though dense fog is likely in the morning.
Twenty scheduled flights were cancelled and four diverted at Birsa Munda Airport on Saturday after weather linked to Cyclone Akvan reduced visibility, airport officials said.
Airport director Vinod Kumar told PTI that visibility remained at around 1,000 metres until 1pm.
Airport officials said aircraft needed between 1,200 and 1,500 metres of visibility for safe take-offs and landings.
Six Air India Express services were among those cancelled.
Jharkhand has experienced overcast skies and light rain since Friday under the influence of the cyclone.
Baburaj PP, director of the Ranchi Meteorological Centre, told PTI that conditions were expected to improve from Sunday, with dense fog likely in the morning.
Clear skies and sunshine are expected from 23 November.
Chaibasa Sadar in West Singhbhum recorded the state’s highest rainfall at 34.4 mm in the 24 hours to 8.30am on Saturday.
Ghatsila received 32.6 mm, followed by Simdega at 28.2 mm, Jamshedpur at 22.2 mm and Ranchi at 12.4 mm.

stories.headline: Navy's Fleet Air Arm: From tracking enemy radars in 1965 to monitoring China along LAC
stories.title: Navy's Fleet Air Arm: From tracking enemy radars in 1965 to monitoring China along LAC
stories.summary: The Indian Navy's Fleet Air Arm has historically supported land operations through naval aviation. Its contribution dates back to the 1965 war, where reconnaissance aircraft identified enemy radar installations. The Boeing 737-based P-8I enhanced these capabilities and was deployed during confrontations with China in recent years. Live feeds from these aircraft aid the Army in monitoring troop movements and strengthening joint operations.

stories.headline: Bulgarian FM lauds India's role in Black Sea peace efforts
stories.title: Bulgarian FM lauds India's role in Black Sea peace efforts
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 21 : Bulgaria's Foreign Minister Velislava Petrova-Chamova on Saturday lauded India's efforts to find a long-term solution to the security situation in the Black Sea region, saying it would help safeguard the movement of essential commodities, including food grains, fertilisers and oil. In her opening remarks during a meeting with External Affairs Minister (EAM) S Jaishankar in New Delhi, Petrova highlighted Bulgaria's role in ensuring the safety of Indian seafarers affected by the escalation of the conflict in the region, involving search and rescue operations. “What one other aspect that really connects us is what we've seen with the escalation of the war in the Black Sea and the security environment that we are part of. It has affected, unfortunately, some of the Indian crew members, and our country has done our best to conduct successful search and rescue and to protect the crew as much as we can,” the Bulgarian FM said. “But of course, we really welcome your efforts in finding a long-term solution there, and very happy to work together with you to find a resolution that not only would improve the security situation there, but also would help those who are in need of the key food and grain products in this case, but also fertilizers, oil, any other products that are needed, and that are at risk because of the harder security situation in the Black Sea,” she added. Highlighting that her visit comes after a gap of 17 years since a Bulgarian Foreign Minister last visited India, Petrova said that this reflected a strong commitment to giving fresh impetus to bilateral relations and strengthening cooperation in multilateral forums. She also welcomed the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA), describing it as a huge achievement and expressing optimism about the opportunities it could create for trade and investment. “We really welcome this and are looking forward to what it is. It was a huge achievement, and I'm glad to say I met with some of your colleagues who worked on this on your side as well. And I was happy to see the commitment to put it into action. It will be important for Europe,” the Bulgarian FM stated. “For us in Bulgaria, as a country that is situated in a way as a gateway to Europe, this could be an opportunity for multiple new interactions, new business relationships, new investments on both sides as well, and ways in which we step on our bilateral relation that historically we've had,” she noted. ( IANS)

stories.headline: CJI Surya Kant calls for guidelines on AI use, disclosure in legal research
stories.title: CJI Surya Kant calls for guidelines on AI use, disclosure in legal research
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Saturday urged the Commonwealth Legal Education Association (CLEA) to develop model guidelines on the disclosure of AI assistance in legal research. Delivering the inaugural address at CLEA 1st Annual International Conference on Legal Education 2026 here, he also suggested that a minimum period of legal aid work be made compulsory for every student to graduate, with additional credits for those who go beyond it. "I would urge CLEA to take the lead by developing model guidelines on the disclosure of AI assistance in legal research, which law schools and journals across the Commonwealth could adapt to their own needs," he said. Talking about research in the age of AI, he cautioned that no student should be held guilty of misconduct on the word of a machine alone as software that claims to tell whether a given essay was written by a student or by a machine can go wrong for different reasons. stories.headline: Karnataka Cabinet clears 15 lakh free sites, one lakh houses
stories.title: Karnataka Cabinet clears 15 lakh free sites, one lakh houses
stories.summary: The decisions were taken at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 19
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Karnataka Cabinet has approved the distribution of 15 lakh free residential sites to landless families and construction of one lakh houses during 2026-27 at an estimated cost of ₹2,241 crore.
The decisions were taken at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 19.
The initiatives aim to provide housing security to families without residential sites and those unable to afford house construction.
Under the proposed Bhooguarantee scheme of the Karnataka government, the first phase will cover five lakh sites at an estimated cost of ₹1,000 crore.

The government plans to develop nine lakh sites in rural areas, requiring around 45,000 acres, while five lakh urban beneficiaries will be accommodated through a G+3 housing model, according to a press release.
The government has identified 23,500 acres of government land across 31 districts, sufficient for about 4.70 lakh sites.
District administrations have been asked to identify additional land.
The first-phase development cost is estimated at ₹20,000 per site.
The proposed Niveshana Yojane will provide sites to eligible landless families, including ex-servicemen, with a 3% reservation for former defence personnel.
Priority will also be given to senior citizens, widows, divorced persons, single mothers, persons with disabilities and transgender persons.
The proposed reservation includes 19.5% for Scheduled Castes and 7.5% for Scheduled Tribes.
The Chief Minister has also directed officials to provide for reservation for Backward Classes.

stories.headline: INS Sahyadri reaches Vietnam to strengthen naval partnership
stories.title: INS Sahyadri reaches Vietnam to strengthen naval partnership
stories.summary: Hanoi, Nov 21: In a move to boost maritime cooperation between India and Vietnam, the Indian Naval Ship (INS) Sahyadri arrived at Tien Sa Port in Da Nang city of the Southeast Asian nation for an operational turnaround. In a post on X on Saturday, the Indian Embassy in Vietnam posted: "The ship was accorded a warm welcome by the Vietnam People's Navy and local authorities. The visit reaffirms our shared commitment to peace, stability and security in the region and in the Indo-Pacific." INS Sahyadri arrived at Tien Sa Port in Da Nang city on Friday for a three-day goodwill visit aimed at deepening defence ties and strengthening naval cooperation between India and Vietnam, local media reported. The Indian Navy frigate was accorded a warm welcome by local authorities, the city's armed forces and the Naval Region 3 Command. The Indian Naval ship, with 294 officers and sailors aboard, will remain in Da Nang until November 22 as part of its goodwill visit, Vietnamese newspaper SGGP reported. As part of the engagements, the Indian Navy delegation will meet the leadership of the Da Nang City People's Committee and the Naval Region 3 Command. The two navies will also participate in sports exchanges involving their officers and personnel. The crew will additionally explore the city's historical and cultural attractions. The visit is expected to promote greater mutual understanding and trust between the two naval forces and deepen defence cooperation between the two countries. Earlier this month, a four-member delegation of the Vietnam People's Army visited the College of Military Engineering (CME) in Pune, as part of the Subject Matter Expert Exchange (SMEE) programme. The visit focused on sharing expertise in combat engineering, counter-IED operations, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) and engineering support to UN Peacekeeping Missions. "Strengthening India-Vietnam Defence Cooperation. A four-member delegation of the Vietnam People's Army visited the College of Military Engineering (#CME), Pune, from 03 to 05 November 2026, as part of the Subject Matter Expert Exchange (SMEE) programme," the Indian Army posted on X. "The visit focused on sharing expertise in combat engineering, counter-IED operations, HADR and engineering support to UN Peacekeeping Missions. The engagement further strengthened professional ties, mutual understanding and bilateral military cooperation between India and Vietnam," it added. Recently, National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval was on an official visit to Vietnam, where he called on Vietnamese President To Lam and thanked him for his 'steadfast support in strengthening the India-Vietnam Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership'. ( IANS)

stories.headline: Abrogation of Article 370 ended separatist sentiments among Kashmiri youth: Shah
stories.title: Abrogation of Article 370 ended separatist sentiments among Kashmiri youth: Shah
stories.summary: Itanagar, Nov 21: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday said that the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019 ended separatist sentiments among Kashmiri youth, and not a single local youth in the Valley is now involved in terrorism after 35 years of violence and unrest. He was addressing an event at Police Training Centre in Banderdewa near Itanagar in which the President's Police Colour was conferred to Arunachal Pradesh Police. "After over 35 years of violence, not a single local youth of Kashmir Valley is now involved in terrorism," he said. Recalling the troubled 90s, he said the situation in Kashmir Valley has undergone a sea change after the abrogation of Article 370. About criticism by opposition parties that the constitutional provision had no connection with terrorism, Shah said developments in the Valley have demonstrated otherwise. He said the change in the Kashmir Valley was brought about not merely by eliminating terrorists but also by ending the atmosphere of discrimination and alienation among the youth of Kashmir. Development activities undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014 had further strengthened the prospects of lasting peace, he added. Shah said the transformation in Kashmir was a matter of immense pride for the country and reflected the sacrifices and dedication of security forces and intelligence agencies. Recalling the turbulent 90s, Shah said terrorism was at its peak and there were doubts about how long the country would be able to hold on to Kashmir. "Even the chief minister of the state had left for England, while security forces, through their courage and sacrifices, ensured that the Valley remained connected with the rest of the country," he said. "Today, from this sacred land of Parshuram ji, I want to tell the entire nation with pride that the abrogation of Article 370 has brought an end to the sense of separatism among the youth of Kashmir. This is reflected in the fact that today, not a single Kashmiri youth is involved in terrorism in Kashmir Valley," he said. Shah said the change in Kashmir was not limited to the elimination of terrorists but also marked a shift in the mindset of the younger generation, with separatist tendencies giving way to hopes of peace and development. He said development in the Valley had gained momentum under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014, adding that the coming years held great promise for Kashmir. The home minister expressed confidence that the transformation in the Valley would pave the way for lasting peace and prosperity, asserting that the experience demonstrated the government's commitment to strengthening national security and promoting development across the country.
